summary: Retest of duplicate_library_material fix (server.py:1880-1939) in the Video Materials feature. Full test_video_materials.py suite now passes 18/18 (was 16/18 in iteration_29). Both previously failing duplicate tests now pass. Also verified end-to-end via ad-hoc script that a duplicated uploaded video (a) gets its own distinct gridfs_id, (b) fires the background transcribe_video_material task, and (c) reaches transcription_status='done' independently of the source.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:1880-1939 duplicate_library_material fix looks clean: correctly branches on is_url_video vs is_video-uploaded vs other, propagates video_url/gridfs_id/transcription_status appropriately, and fires asyncio.create_task(transcribe_video_material(new_material_id)) only when a new GridFS blob was actually written. Confirmed behaviorally.

Minor: transcript field is hard-reset to '' for uploaded-video duplicates even though the original may already have a transcript. Since background re-transcription is scheduled, this is correct but slightly wasteful for large videos — consider copying the transcript and skipping re-transcription in a future optimization. Not blocking.
410 handling on read_bytes_from_doc during duplicate is now explicit — nice defensive re-raise.

rca of the issue: Previous iteration_29 failure RCA: duplicate_library_material assumed all materials had a GridFS file and did not propagate video-specific fields. Fix: added is_video/is_url_video branching, skip GridFS copy for URL videos (video_url preserved, transcription_status='n/a'), for uploaded videos copy GridFS bytes + set transcription_status='pending' + schedule background transcription. Verified: both automated tests pass and manual end-to-end run shows duplicate reaches independent 'done' state with distinct gridfs_id.
